title: Strategic Air Command letter congratulating the Necronomicon publishers

tellings.quote: And then the SA the street of air command SACE came in with a letter you know just a nice letter saying congratulations on your new publication.
But Lavenda has said that he's personally received letters from inside the US military praising the Necronomicon for being {quote} spot on,
tellings.difference: Speaks of several letters, adds Fort Benning, and says the military called the book 'spot on' where the story has a simple congratulations.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell of Levenda receiving military praise, including from Strategic Air Command, for his Necronomicon.

plain: In the late 1970s, according to the author Peter Levenda, Strategic Air Command, the part of the US Air Force that ran the nuclear bombers and missiles, sent a friendly letter on its own letterhead congratulating the publishers of the Necronomicon, a book of supposed ancient magic spells that Levenda helped bring out. Levenda says he saw this himself, and he names a man called Larry Barnes in telling it. Michels repeats the story in another episode in a bigger form: he says Levenda received several letters from inside the military, mentions Fort Benning, an Army base, and says they praised the book as "spot on", where Levenda describes just a simple note of congratulations.
